mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% and remains >4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the triggered period, or FEDFUNDS does not sustain the level for two months.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, labor market slack increases, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment period, or UNRATE does not remain below 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST (household spending index) of at least 2% for two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the two-month up-trend, or the increase in HOUST is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the supply contraction, or INDPRO recovers within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a single month, it reflects accelerating inflation expectations and predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the month of high CPIAUCSL growth.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in PAYEMS (employment months) suggests weakening labor market absorption, which interacts with FEDFUNDS to produce a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return when FEDFUNDS is below 4%.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases for two months AND FEDFUNDS < 4% for the same period
regime_hint: labor softening coupled with loose policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both triggers are met, or interaction rank IC < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 3% each over a 5-day window predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via stronger economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases ≥3% in one month AND RSAFS increases ≥3% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the momentum window, or either proxy does not meet the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to post-recession supply expansion (indicated by INDPRO crossing above 105 and remaining above for 3 months) is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the supply expansion, or INDPRO does not sustain the level for three months.
